- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior period), model often overshoots; apply a 3–7 day lag correction, dampening forecast by 10–20% in following days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates; adjust upward by 3–8% to capture mean reversion.
- In periods with mixed sentiment (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture volatility; apply a 1–3% smoothing filter to reduce overfitting.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; use 7-day moving average of sentiment to weight forecast adjustments.
- If recent history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), model should be adjusted downward by 1–4% per day to avoid overcorrection.
